channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts Conference on Strengthening State Cooperation with Overseas Diasporas
item.description: A national conference on engaging Tajik diasporas and compatriots abroad as development partners was held in Dushanbe. Organized by the Ministry of Labor, Migration and Employment, the event aimed to foster dialogue and leverage the potential of diasporas for sustainable national development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan implements six-month ban on certain construction material imports
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has imposed a temporary six-month ban on the import of specific construction materials. This measure aims to protect domestic manufacturers, stabilize the local market, and ensure economic and national security against foreign competition.

item.title: Uzbekistan's economy grew 8.5% in first half of 2026, budget deficit at 0.7% of GDP
item.description: Uzbekistan's consolidated budget deficit was 0.7% of GDP in the first half of 2026. The economy grew 8.5%, driven by services, construction, industry, investment, and exports. Annual inflation stood at 6.4%.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes 'cooperation for rapid development' vision with Central Asia and South Korea
item.description: Uzbekistan has proposed developing a long-term conceptual vision titled 'Central Asia - Republic of Korea: Cooperation for Rapid Development'. The initiative was put forward by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the first summit between the region's countries and South Korea in Seoul.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Customs Disrupt Synthetic Drug Smuggling Channel in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Northern Railway Customs and the Interior Ministry's anti-drug service have dismantled an illegal mephedrone smuggling operation in Bishkek. An 18-year-old woman was detained with a large quantity of the synthetic drug, which could have generated over 10 million soms.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Monthly Allowances for Medical Personnel Starting January 1
item.description: Starting January 1, certain medical professionals in Uzbekistan will receive monthly allowances based on their qualifications. Graduates of bachelor's programs will receive one minimum wage, master's graduates two, and family medicine specialists four.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sees Decline in Private Housing Construction in August
item.description: In January-August, Kyrgyzstan commissioned 6,009 private homes totaling 822,900 square meters, with investments reaching 26.2 billion soms. However, housing area put into operation decreased by 0.7% compared to the previous year, reversing a positive trend.

item.title: Vietnamese ROX Group Considers Major Investment Projects in Uzbekistan
item.description: Vietnam's ROX Group is exploring new investment projects in several regions of Uzbekistan, including Bukhara, Samarkand, and Jizzakh. In Bukhara, a project valued at $2 billion aims to construct modern real estate, residential areas, schools, and infrastructure on over 85 hectares, potentially creating 5,000-6,000 jobs and improving housing for over 50,000 citizens.

item.title: Gender Stereotypes Impacting Justice System in Uzbekistan, Expert Claims
item.description: An expert on gender issues and founder of the Nemolchi.uz anti-violence project in Uzbekistan, Irina Matvienko, criticizes a court ruling that blamed a victim of domestic violence for the crime. Matvienko argues such phrasing reflects gender stereotypes, leading to victim-blaming and potentially influencing how the state portrays violence.

item.title: New Monthly Allowances for Nurses and Family Doctors in Uzbekistan Effective 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan has established a system for paying monthly allowances to nurses and family doctors. Starting January 1, 2027, nurses and medical assistants who complete master's degrees will receive a monthly allowance equivalent to twice the minimum wage, while those with bachelor's degrees will receive one times the minimum wage.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Five Initiatives to Boost Central Asia-South Korea Cooperation
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev put forward five proposals to develop cooperation between Central Asia and South Korea. These initiatives focus on long-term partnership, trade and investment, critical minerals, green development, and human capital development. The proposals aim to strengthen regional ties and economic collaboration.

item.title: Uzbekistan Tightens Admission and Training Requirements for Medical and Pharmaceutical Fields
item.description: Uzbekistan has significantly tightened admission and training requirements for medical and pharmaceutical fields, according to a presidential decree. The new measures aim to fundamentally improve the system of training personnel in these sectors, introducing strict criteria for admissions, exam scores, and study procedures.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Maintains Key Interest Rate at 14% Amid Inflationary Risks
item.description: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has kept its key interest rate unchanged at 14% annually. Despite a downward trend in inflation and signs of economic rebalancing, the regulator cited persistent risks that could increase inflation, necessitating the continuation of current tight monetary conditions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Faces High Risk of Nitazenes, Synthetic Opioids, Despite No Detections Yet
item.description: Uzbekistan faces a high risk of nitazenes, synthetic opioids hundreds of times stronger than heroin, despite no confirmed cases. Customs seized nearly 1.9 tons of drugs in early 2024, but nitazenes were absent. The committee considers the risk high due to global drug market shifts, including China's control over fentanyl-like substances and Afghanistan's poppy cultivation ban.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes gradual pension age increase starting 2028
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Economy and Finance proposed a gradual increase in the retirement age, starting in 2028. The plan aims to raise the age to 63 for men and 58 for women by 2039. Measures are included to protect pre-retirement workers and allow early pension access for the unemployed.

item.title: Hong Kong unveils first five-year socio-economic development plan
item.description: Hong Kong has presented its first five-year socio-economic development plan, aiming to consolidate and enhance its advantages in international finance, shipping, trade, innovation, and technology. The plan seeks to integrate the region more effectively into China's overall development and support the "one country, two systems" policy.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank keeps key interest rate at 14 percent
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has maintained its key interest rate at 14 percent. The regulator cited the need to continue current tight monetary and credit conditions due to persistent inflationary risks. The decision aims to stabilize prices and support economic growth.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan updates migration rules for Tajik citizens
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has updated its migration regulations. The changes specify new procedures for citizens of Tajikistan. Information regarding the updated requirements for Tajik nationals is now available.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Approves Public Works for Repeated Waste Violations
item.description: The Jogorku Kenesh approved amendments to the Code of Offenses, introducing public works for repeat offenders of waste disposal and cleanliness rules. First-time offenders face a warning or fines. Repeat violations within a year, such as illegal dumping or burning of waste after a prior fine, will result in 20-30 hours of public work.

item.title: Tajikistan Delegation Attends 70th IAEA General Conference in Vienna
item.description: A delegation from Tajikistan is participating in the 70th General Conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in Vienna, running from September 14-18. The delegation is led by Deputy Foreign Minister Nigina Alizoda and includes officials from the Ministry of Industry and New Technologies and the National Academy of Sciences. Discussions will focus on the safe and peaceful use of nuclear technologies.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Proposes Joint Medical Center and Easier Visa Rules with South Korea
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov proposed establishing a joint medical center in Kyrgyzstan and easing visa regulations with South Korea during talks with his South Korean counterpart. Discussions also covered trade, investment, and infrastructure projects. Japarov invited the South Korean president to visit Kyrgyzstan, suggesting timing it with the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations.

item.title: Uzbekistan introduces "5+1" medical bachelor's program, abolishes narrow specialization master's
item.description: Uzbekistan is introducing a six-year "5+1" general medical bachelor's program based on the "Treatment of Diseases" specialty. Graduates will receive a general practitioner qualification and can work as family doctors. The master's programs for narrow specializations are being abolished.

item.title: Part of Bishkek to experience 10-hour water supply suspension on September 17
item.description: A section of Bishkek will be without drinking water from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. on September 17 due to maintenance at the Airport water intake facility. The outage will affect the old airport area, Chingiz Aitmatov Avenue, and nearby streets, impacting residential buildings, schools, and healthcare facilities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Proposes International Committee for World Nomad Games
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan, Tabyldy Muratbekov, has proposed the creation of an international committee for the World Nomad Games. He stated that the games have become a key feature of Kyrgyzstan, increasing international interest in the country. The proposed committee aims to systematically promote the history, culture, and national sports of nomadic peoples worldwide.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Demands Urgent Inspection of School Coal Quality Amid Safety Concerns
item.description: Kyrgyzstan MP Tabyldy Muratbekov has called for an urgent inspection of coal supplied to schools after instances of spontaneous combustion were reported. He noted that poor coal quality or other factors could pose a safety risk. Muratbekov urged for laboratory analysis of the fuel and prevention of hazardous coal delivery to schools.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Bahrain Discuss Launching Direct Flights Between Tashkent and Manama
item.description: Uzbekistan and Bahrain are discussing the possibility of launching direct flights between Tashkent and Manama. The issue was addressed during a meeting between the Chairman of the Uzbekistan Tourism Committee and the Minister of Tourism of Bahrain. Both sides also agreed to enhance mutual tourist flows and strengthen direct ties between tourism industry representatives.

item.title: UN Resident Coordinator Antje Grawe concludes mission in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: UN Resident Coordinator Antje Grawe is concluding her four-year mission in Kyrgyzstan. She met with the Minister of Labor, Social Security and Migration to discuss cooperation in social protection, employment, and labor migration.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP urges inspection of school coal quality amid safety concerns
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan has called for an urgent inspection of coal supplied to schools due to instances of smoldering and self-ignition. Tabлды Муратбеков stated that school staff are attempting to manage the issue by moving or wetting the coal, but this sometimes exacerbates the problem. He emphasized the need for safety checks and clear instructions for schools.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan border guards honored at Ata-Beyit memorial complex
item.description: A ceremony was held at the Ata-Beyit memorial complex to honor military personnel who died defending the state border during clashes on the Kyrgyz-Tajik section in 2021 and 2022. The State Border Service reported that approximately 100 people died on the Kyrgyz side in these conflicts.

item.title: Zelenskyy: Russian drones flew twice near his plane over Moldova
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russian drones flew twice near his aircraft while it was over Moldova. He described the incident as a near-miss encounter with a drone.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Six-Year "5+1" Bachelor's Degree in Medicine from 2027/28
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce a six-year "5+1" bachelor's degree in medicine starting from the 2027/2028 academic year. The program will include a full year of practical training for final-year students. The Ministry of Health will approve state order parameters based on current and future needs for medical personnel.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Meets South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon met with South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo in Seoul. They discussed expanding bilateral cooperation in industry, energy, agriculture, transport, finance, and digitalization. Both sides expressed interest in strengthening economic and investment ties and activating joint mechanisms.

item.title: Tajikistan President Emomali Rahmon Holds High-Level Talks in South Korea
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon met with South Korean leadership in Seoul on September 16 during an official visit. Discussions focused on strengthening bilateral cooperation, with both sides emphasizing historical ties and shared values. Priority areas for collaboration include trade, economy, investment, energy, transport, digitalization, agriculture, and tourism.

item.title: Dushanbe Discusses Satellite Communications Development with Chinese Specialists
item.description: Dushanbe hosted a meeting between specialists from Tajikistan's Communications Service and Chinese experts from the China Academy of Space Technology and other companies. The discussion focused on developing satellite communications, implementing modern space technologies, and enhancing technical exchange to improve Tajikistan's telecommunications sector.

item.title: Korea and Kyrgyzstan Elevate Relations to Comprehensive Partnership
item.description: Bilateral relations between the Republic of Korea and the Kyrgyz Republic reached a new level in December 2024, becoming a comprehensive partnership. Cooperation now spans development aid, trade, investment, digital transformation, and climate action, building on existing exchanges.

item.title: Khorezm Region to Attract $100 Million Investment for Waste-to-Energy Project
item.description: The Khorezm region will attract $100 million in investments for a project to generate electricity from waste. "Uzenergosotish" will purchase the electricity produced under the project for 30 years with guaranteed terms.

item.title: China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway to Boost Eurasian Trade
item.description: The construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is a key event for Central Asia, according to Mukhtor Umarov, Chairman of the Uzbekistan Economic Assembly. He stated that connecting this line with the Middle Corridor and the Trans-Afghan route will significantly shorten logistics and position Uzbekistan as a major Eurasian trade hub.

item.title: Biosecurity Crucial for Central Asia Amid Global Changes, Expert Says
item.description: Kairat Tabyanov, a virologist and biosecurity specialist at the Regional Environmental Center for Central Asia (CAREC), emphasizes the growing importance of biosecurity due to global changes and trade. He focuses on zoonoses, infections transferable from animals to humans, and consults on a World Bank project related to veterinary biosecurity.
